bugs: Wrapping /api routes in the 'web' middleware group (routes/api.php:6) applies session and CSRF checks to the JSON API. Tests skip CSRF, but a real client would get 419 on POST/PUT/DELETE unless it does the SPA cookie+token handshake.
An empty filter (?status=) returns 422 instead of being ignored. impl-2 and impl-3 behave the same way, so this is minor.
antipatterns: routes/api.php:6: the 'web' group is mixed into the API route file.

app/Http/Requests/StorePostRequest.php:22-32: prepareForValidation trims tags by hand, but the global TrimStrings middleware already does this (the probe confirmed ' php' vs 'php' is already caught as a duplicate). This is dead ceremony.

app/Http/Requests/UpdatePostRequest.php:5-15: it extends StorePostRequest only to reuse parent::rules()['status'] and the trim hook, then redeclares every other rule. The inheritance is awkward and adds nothing.

app/Http/Requests/UpdatePostRequest.php:10: title uses 'sometimes' without 'required'. It only rejects '' because ConvertEmptyStringsToNull turns it into null first, so the rule depends on middleware it doesn't state.
strengths: Modern model attributes: #[Fillable], #[ObservedBy], #[Scope]. Also casts() method, a backed enum, and Rule::enum.
Thin controller: user()->posts() scoping, when() filters, latest()->latest('id') as a tiebreaker, and withQueryString pagination.
Policy uses $post->user()->is($user), and the controller calls Gate::authorize.
The observer handles the unique slug, falls back to 'post' for titles that produce no slug, and sets published_at only when it is missing.
whenLoaded tags mapped to names. Missing tags are kept on update and an empty array clears them.
A solid set of 20 tests. They cover validation messages, 403, 404, pagination meta, filter combinations, and keeping published_at when republishing.

bugs: An empty filter (?status=) returns 422 instead of being ignored. This is shared by all three implementations and is minor.
antipatterns: app/Http/Requests/StorePostRequest.php:25-28 and UpdatePostRequest.php:25-28: the postAttributes() wrapper around safe()->except('tags') is duplicated in both requests. It is one-line ceremony that could just be inlined.
app/Models/Post.php:34-37: getRouteKeyName() override, where Laravel 13 has the #[RouteKey] attribute. The model uses attributes everywhere else, so this is inconsistent.
tests/Feature/PostApiTest.php:21: Http::preventStrayRequests() is noise, because the feature makes no HTTP calls.
tests/Feature/PostApiTest.php:311-314: test_status_is_cast_to_enum only tests the framework's cast.
strengths: Clean apiResource routes, so both PUT and PATCH work. Route-model binding uses the slug, which stays stable because the slug is never regenerated.
'sometimes','required' in the update rules states the intent directly. tags.* is required|string|distinct.
The observer uses ??= for both the slug and published_at, which is concise and correct.
DRY policy: delete() delegates to update().
26 tests. They cover mass-assignment protection (user_id, slug, published_at), keeping published_at across draft→published cycles, the default page size, and filter combinations.

bugs: PATCH /api/posts/{post} returns 405 (routes/api.php:9 registers only PUT). Every update field is 'sometimes', so updates are partial in practice, yet the conventional PATCH verb isn't routed.
An empty filter (?status=) returns 422 instead of being ignored. This is shared and minor.
antipatterns: routes/api.php:7-10: the four routes are written by hand instead of apiResource()->except('show'). As a result they have no route names and no PATCH.

app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:35: ->response()->setStatusCode(201) is redundant. A JsonResource already returns 201 for a model with wasRecentlyCreated, and the JsonResponse return type is noisier than returning PostResource.
app/Http/Requests/IndexPostRequest.php:22: PostStatus::tryFrom((string) ...) is a hand-rolled version of $request->enum().
tests/Feature/PostApiTest.php:338-341: the test only checks the framework's enum cast.
strengths: Route-level ->can('update','post') authorization keeps the controller free of auth calls and returns 403 before validation. A dedicated test checks this.
The nullable scopes (withStatus(?PostStatus), taggedWith(?string)) use when() internally, so the controller reads as a fluent chain.
syncTagNames dedupes with ->unique(), so duplicate tag names are accepted gracefully rather than rejected.
The most thorough suite, with 30 tests. They cover length limits, tags kept after delete, 404 on update and delete, unpublish, and the default page size.
The same modern attribute-based model, enum cast, and observer approach as the others.

v.rationale:
I ran each suite and probed all three. They passed their own suites (20, 26 and 30 tests) and behaved the same in my probes for null fields, slug collisions, titles made only of symbols, unicode titles, invalid tags, keeping published_at, and other users' posts being isolated. Because they are so close, the ranking comes down to small routing and idiom differences.

impl-2 ranks first. It uses apiResource, so both PUT and PATCH work, and route binding uses the slug. It reads the status filter with $request->enum, writes update rules as 'sometimes','required', and uses ??= in the observer. Its flaws are small: postAttributes() is duplicated in two requests, and it uses getRouteKeyName() instead of the #[RouteKey] attribute.

impl-3 ranks second. It has the most thorough tests, an elegant route-level ->can() check, and nullable when() scopes. But its hand-written routes drop PATCH (405), and it adds redundant 201 handling and a tryFrom helper.

impl-1 ranks third. It is functionally solid, but it adds the 'web' middleware group (session plus CSRF) to the API routes. It also has a dead prepareForValidation trim, since TrimStrings already does that, and an awkward UpdatePostRequest-extends-StorePostRequest inheritance that redeclares almost every rule.
